traits.flower_symmetry.note: Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 475), Mimosaceae: small regular mostly perfect flowers; Acacia, which then held Senegalia: flowers small, in heads or spikes, stamens many, exserted, filaments filiform, distinct. Kearney and Peebles (1942): stamens many more than 10.

traits.stamens.note: Brenan's Flora of Tropical East Africa account of Mimosoideae (1959, p. 49), Acacia in the old wide sense that held Senegalia: stamens many, 35 to about 215 in the East African species; Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 475): stamens many, exserted. No figure for Senegalia alone.

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Abrams (vol. 2, 1944, p. 475), Acacia (then holding Senegalia): stamens many, exserted; filaments filiform, distinct.
